newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Indians protest against copper mining.
newsitem.headline: Panama Indians protest against copper mining.

text.p: Several hundred members of Panama's largest group of Indians marched to the presidential palace on Wednesday to demand an end to copper mining on their lands and the creation of their own homeland.

Wearing traditional dress and face paint, Ngobe-Bugle Indians shouted "No to mining!" and "Down with the president!" outside the palace, where President Ernesto Perez Balladares was meeting with his Cabinet.

The Ngobe-Bugle Indians, the largest of Panama's six Indian groups, with a population of 125,000, were protesting against Perez Balladares' decision to back copper mining on their lands in Cerro Colorado, 220 miles (350 km) from Panama City. The site is believed to have the world's 12th-largest copper deposit.
The Indians want the mining project stopped and their lands declared sovereign and independent. They have been pressing for an Indian territory for 25 years.
The Cabinet was expected to discuss the territorial proposal.
